names: P11A -- traffic median (half-circle island near Mission Bay Circle)
summary: A grass, semicircular traffic median immediately east of the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout, west of the Parklab Gardens soccer field; a real, already-landscaped median island per satellite imagery, hand-traced with the property owner's guidance and fit to an idealized semicircle. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P11/11A' together among the parcels already managed by SF Recreation and Parks (not among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date.

milestones.text: Already part of RPD's managed open-space inventory as 'P11/11A' (not listed among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), per OCII's Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation to the Mission Bay CAC -- an upper bound on when this median was built, not its actual construction date

images.credit: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency, NAIP aerial imagery (2024 flight), via USDA's 'latest NAIP' image service
images.license_note: USDA's data.gov catalog record for NAIP imagery sets the license to the U.S. government public-domain label (usa.gov/publicdomain/label/1.0); the USDA FSA policies page says public-domain information may be freely distributed with credit requested ('U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency'). Read 2026-09-22.
images.caption: USDA NAIP aerial orthophoto (2024 flight), cropped to the Mission Bay project area and its immediate surroundings
images.appeal_note: A straight-down orthophoto rather than an oblique aerial, but Oracle Park and Chase Center are both clearly recognizable landmarks in the frame, giving anyone who knows the city an immediate fix on the neighborhood.

images.credit: Firstcultural (Alfred Twu), aerial view from a departing flight, via Wikimedia Commons; CC0; downscaled to 1600 px
images.license_note: Wikimedia Commons' license box on the file page confirms CC0 (public domain dedication) by Firstcultural (Alfred Twu). Read 2026-09-23.
images.caption: Aerial view of Mission Bay, Oracle Park and the Caltrain/King Street area from a departing flight
images.appeal_note: Oracle Park's diamond and Chase Center's dome (with its own logo) are both clearly identifiable landmarks in one colorful frame -- reads far better at card size than the flatter government orthophoto.

sources.title: Mission Bay Parks Open Space (CAC Item 2, September 2023)
sources.publisher: Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (sfocii.org)

open_questions: No public source names this specific median island or gives its own construction date; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes it existed and was already RPD-managed by that date (grouped with P11), which is an upper bound, not a build date.

This record was previously only a weak ~33m proximity guess with no real source before the property owner drew its actual outline directly on a satellite screenshot (per this record's own digitization_method log); the P-number itself, and any name/operator, remain unconfirmed by any independent published source.
